name: Ortona
title: Ortona Ship Gauging: UTM for Coasters and Small Cargo Ships
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging in Ortona for coasters, small bulk and general cargo ships, tugs and workboats: hold, deck, tank and hull steel readings.
h1: Hull Thickness Measurement in Ortona, Abruzzo
intro: Ortona is a modest Adriatic port in Abruzzo, serving industrial cargo for the region and a fleet of coasters, small bulk carriers, tugs and workboats. Few ships stay long, and a drydock is not always at hand, so gauging has to be planned tightly. Atlantis NDT sends technicians from India to the ship, with no one based on the Abruzzo coast, and builds each job around the cargo stop, the harbour's draught limits and the repair yard nearby.

highlights.p: Ortona's quays suit short-sea ships carrying steel, aggregates, cement and project cargo, so most jobs involve compact holds, hatch covers and ballast tanks on ships that rarely stay for more than a cargo stop.

highlights.h: A small yard for local craft
highlights.p: The port has a repair yard serving local workboats, tugs and fishing craft, which makes steel condition checks possible alongside or on a slipway when owners want a record before a repair or a sale.
Draught limits and the need for periodic dredging keep ship size modest, so gauging teams work with handy-sized tonnage and plan around the depth available at the berth on the day.

port.h: The port of Ortona: a working harbour on the Abruzzo coast
p: Ortona stands on a headland on the Adriatic coast of Abruzzo, between Pescara to the north and Vasto to the south. The port lies below the old town behind a breakwater system that shelters a compact basin with commercial quays on its inner side and a marina and fishing section at one end. It belongs to the Central Adriatic port authority together with Ancona and the other Marche and Abruzzo ports. Ships approach from open Adriatic water, and because the coast is exposed to northerly and north-easterly winds, bora and levante conditions occasionally keep smaller ships outside until the swell drops.

The commercial traffic is regional and varied rather than large. Coasters bring and take steel products, cement, aggregates, fertiliser, agricultural goods and project cargo for the industrial zones of Abruzzo, and ferries to the Croatian coast have run from the port in the past. Silting at the entrance and along the quays is a recurring concern and the authority carries out dredging, which means the maximum draught available at a berth can vary from season to season. The ships that call are therefore mostly small to medium coasters and handy-sized bulk and general cargo vessels.

Smaller ships bring a distinct profile to thickness gauging. Many are older and have worked in short-sea trades for decades, with coating breakdown in ballast tanks and wastage around hatch coamings and cargo hold bottoms. The port also hosts tugs, pilot boats, fishing vessels and workboats whose owners need a condition record for insurers, charterers or buyers. These jobs are usually short and defined, a single hold, a ballast tank group or a hull belt, and the results are often needed quickly after the cargo stop so that the ship can sail on schedule.

facilities.h: Where gauging happens in Ortona: quays, the repair yard and lay-by berths
p: Most gauging is performed alongside at the commercial quays while cargo is being worked or immediately afterwards. Holds are measured once empty and safe for entry, with the stevedores' schedule dictating when each space becomes available. Because the ships are small, a single team can often cover holds, deck, hatch covers and an accessible ballast tank group in one working day. We plan the sequence with the master, so that spaces needed first are measured first and a late discharge does not lose the whole window.

A small repair yard in the port works on local tugs, workboats and fishing craft, and can handle slipway or floating-dock work on small hulls, but it is not a destination for large merchant ships. For a full renewal survey on a coaster, owners often book a yard elsewhere in the Adriatic, such as Ancona, Ravenna or a Croatian yard, and a measured survey in Ortona beforehand lets that yard plan steel renewal. Ships that lie idle or wait for a cargo can use a lay-by berth, which gives time for an owner's condition check of the full hull and tanks.
list: Commercial quays — hold frames, tank tops, hatch covers and coamings of coasters and small bulk carriers once cargo is out
Berths for steel and project cargo — deck, hatch cover and cross-deck structure readings on multipurpose ships between loading windows
The port's repair yard — hull plating of tugs, pilot boats and workboats on the slipway or in the dock, where the yard allows access
Lay-by berths — owner's condition checks on ships awaiting employment or sale, covering ballast tanks and the shell
Anchorage off the port — occasional condition checks on ships waiting for a berth, in calm sea conditions through the agent

context.h: Port state control and regulation for small ships in Ortona
p: Port state control in Ortona is exercised by the Italian Coast Guard through the harbour master (Capitaneria di Porto), under the Paris MoU. Small coasters and older general cargo ships tend to carry a higher ship risk profile, so they are boarded more often than newer tonnage, and structural findings such as wasted coamings or corroded hold bottoms are common reasons for deficiencies. Many ships of this size are not subject to the full ESP programme but still follow their class society's renewal and intermediate survey requirements, and the class surveyor decides what readings are needed for each survey.

The wider regulatory frame also applies. The EU Ship Recycling Regulation requires an Inventory of Hazardous Materials on ships calling at EU ports, and owners of older coasters thinking about sale or scrapping value a record of remaining steel. EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime shape the economics of keeping small ships in service, since the fleet is often old and fuel-intensive. For fishing vessels and workboats, which are not always classed, insurers and buyers frequently ask for independent thickness records, and a short gauging survey in Ortona can supply them without a trip to a larger port.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Ortona
jobs.p: Ortona jobs are small, defined and usually fitted around a cargo stop. A coaster may be alongside for a day, a tug may be on the quay for a week, and the aim is to gather the readings the surveyor, the insurer or the buyer actually needs. We agree the list of spaces, permits and the reporting format with the owner or superintendent before the technicians travel from India, and leave a remaining list for the next call.
list: Hold bottom, frame and hatch coaming gauging on a coaster after steel discharge, ahead of an intermediate survey
Ballast tank readings on a small general cargo ship at the quay, so a yard in Ancona or Ravenna can plan steel renewal
Hull plating survey of a tug on the port's slipway before a repair or change of ownership
Owner's condition gauging of a workboat or fishing vessel for an insurer, with a short report on the weakest areas
Pre-purchase gauging of a small bulk carrier at a lay-by berth, covering holds, deck and accessible tanks

logistics: Pescara Airport is the nearest airport to Ortona, with limited services, so teams usually travel through Rome, Bologna or Bari and continue by road or rail. The ship's agent arranges port access and any launch needed for anchorage work, and for small ships that are not under agency it is the owner who books the berth and clears the team through the gate. Our technicians are Indian nationals travelling on Schengen visas, so we start the application when the job is confirmed and book flights once the ship's schedule at Ortona is firm.
vessels: Coasters and short-sea general cargo ships

faqs.q: Is it worth gauging a small coaster in Ortona rather than waiting for a yard?
faqs.a: Often yes. Readings taken alongside tell the owner where steel is wasted before the ship goes to a yard, so the yard can estimate renewal from measured figures and the owner can decide between repair, sale and scrapping. For small ships a single day's work frequently covers holds, deck and the accessible ballast tanks.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a tug or workboat on a slipway in Ortona?
faqs.a: Yes, where the yard allows access. With the hull out of the water, we can measure plating, the bottom and the area around rudders and stern gear, after surface cleaning. We agree with the yard which areas are cleaned and when, so the readings are taken on prepared steel and recorded with its condition.

faqs.q: Do draught limits at Ortona affect the gauging job?
faqs.a: They affect which ships call, not the gauging method. Because available depth at the berths changes with silting and dredging, ships are generally small to medium coasters. We plan around the ship's draught and berth, and if a ship has to lighten or wait outside, we adjust the sequence of spaces to the time actually available.

faqs.q: What documents does a small ship need for a thickness survey?
faqs.a: The superintendent supplies the class survey status, the gauging plan or tank drawings if available, and any previous thickness reports. For ships without class, we agree the scope with the owner and the insurer or buyer. We report readings by location with a plan, so any later survey can compare against the same points.

faqs.q: Can gauging in Ortona be combined with work in Ancona or Pescara?
faqs.a: Yes. Ships often call at several Adriatic ports in a single rotation, and one mobilisation can cover more than one berth if the schedules allow. Send us the ship's itinerary when you enquire, and we will sequence the work so that the team is not waiting between calls.
